gloss: to pin a crime on someone; to frame someone

definitions.gloss: to pin a crime on someone; to frame someone; to shift the blame
definitions.explanation: To make someone else take the blame for something they did not do. Literally means to "put guilt/crime on top of someone." Used for both serious criminal framing and everyday blame-shifting.

examples.japanese: {他人|たにん}に{罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}せた。
examples.english: He pinned the blame on someone else.

examples.japanese: {無実|むじつ}の{人|ひと}に{罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}せるのは{許|ゆる}せない。
examples.english: It's unforgivable to frame an innocent person.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{失敗|しっぱい}の{罪|つみ}を{部下|ぶか}に{被|かぶ}せるような{上司|じょうし}は{信頼|しんらい}されない。
examples.english: A boss who pins the blame for their own failures on subordinates won't be trusted.

notes:
Composed of {罪|つみ} (crime, guilt, blame) + を (object marker) + {被|かぶ}せる (to put on top of, to cover with). The verb {被|かぶ}せる literally means to place something over or on top of someone, like putting a hat on them — here, the "crime" is placed on them. Compare with {罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}る (to take the blame), where the person themselves "wears" the guilt.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}せられる: to have the blame pinned on oneself (passive)
- {無実|むじつ}の{人|ひと}に{罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}せる: to frame an innocent person
- {他人|たにん}に{罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}せる: to pin blame on others

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {罪|つみ}を{着|き}せる: to frame, to accuse falsely — very similar in meaning; uses the metaphor of "dressing" someone in guilt
- {罪|つみ}を{被|かぶ}る: to take the blame — the inverse; the person accepts the guilt themselves
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}を{着|き}せる: to put a false charge on someone — a more literary expression meaning to falsely accuse
